title: PUCN Order — Docket 26-04015 (2026-07-08)
text:
BEFORE THE PUBLIC UTILITIES COMMISSION OF NEVADA

Annual Report of Switch Ltd. on compliance with the )
Portfolio Standard for Renewable Energy for

) Docket No. 26-04015
Compliance Year 2025. )
)

At a general session of the Public Utilities
Commission of Nevada, held at its offices
on June 30, 2026.

PRESENT: Chair Hayley Williamson
Commissioner Tammy Cordova
Commissioner Randy J. Brown
Assistant Commission Secretary Trisha Osborne

ORDER
The Public Utilities Commission of Nevada (“Commission”) makes the following
findings of fact and conclusions of law:
I. INTRODUCTION

On April 13, 2026, Switch Ltd. (“Switch”) filed with the Commission an annual report,
designated as Docket No. 26-04015, on compliance with the renewable energy portfolio standard
(“RPS”) for compliance year 2025 (the “Compliance Year”).

I. SUMMARY

The Commission approves the annual report and finds that Switch has complied with the
RPS requirements for 2025.

Ii. PROCEDURAL HISTORY

* On April 13, 2026, Switch filed the annual report pursuant to the Nevada Revised Statutes
(“NRS”) and the Nevada Administrative Code (“NAC”) Chapters 703 and 704, including, but
not limited to, NRS 704.7825, NAC 704.8877, and NAC 704.8879, additionally, Switch requests
confidential treatment of certain information contained in its annual report pursuant to NRS
703.190 and NAC 703.527 et seq.

* On April 17, 2026, the Commission issued a Notice of Electric Provider’s Annual Report on
Compliance with the Nevada Renewable Energy Portfolio Standard.

* The Regulatory Operations Staff of the Commission (“Staff”) participates as a matter of right
pursuant to NRS 703.301.

Docket No. 26-04015 Page 2

* On June 25, 2026, Staff filed a briefing memorandum (“Staff Briefing Memo”).
IV. ANNUAL REPORT
Switch’s Position

1, Switch states it is committed to being 100% green and meets the RPS statutory
requirement for the Compliance Year, and that based upon NV Energy’s monthly usage bills,
Switch’s Compliance Year Nevada load is 1,397,988 megawatt-hour (“MWh”), and Switch
retired sufficient portfolio energy credits (“PECs”)/renewable energy credits to meet 100% of its
load in this Compliance Year. (Annual Report at 1.)

Staff's Position

2. Staff states that Switch takes retail service from Tenaska Power Services Co.
(“Tenaska”) pursuant to NRS 704B, and Tenaska, therefore, is a “Provider of Electric Service”
as defined in NRS 704.7808 and must comply with the Nevada RPS set forth in NRS 704.78213,
but that on April 13, 2026, Tenaska filed its Annual Report (Docket No. 26-04014) which
acknowledges that Switch filed the present Annual Report to also demonstrate Tenaska's
compliance with its RPS requirements for the retail sales it made to Switch. (Staff Briefing
Memo at 1.)

3. Staff states that pursuant to the provisions of NRS 704.78213, Tenaska is required
to meet the RPS requirements that were set forth in NRS 704.7821, and under the provisions of
NRS 704.7821(1)(j), the RPS requirement for compliance year 2025 stands at 34 percent of total
retail sales. (/d. at 2.)

4. Staff states that for the Compliance Year, Switch’s total load was 1,397,988
MWh, accordingly, Switch is required to acquire and retire PECs equal to 475,316 MWh

(475,316,000 PECs) on behalf of its provider for the 2025 RPS. (/d.)

Docket No. 26-04015 Page 3

5. Staff states that Switch summarizes its portfolio credit position in Section II of its
Compliance Report, as Switch received 438,462,000 PECs in the Compliance Year from Switch
Station 1 and 2 pursuant to agreements under NV Energy’s Green Rider Program, and states that
it retired additional credits to cover its entire compliance year load of 1,397,988 MWh, and
Switch is not requesting to carry forward PECs on behalf of Tenaska at this time. (/d.)

6. Staff states that in previous dockets pertaining to Switch’s annual reports, the
Commission has issued orders containing directives for Switch to provide copies of monthly
invoices or other verification to support the claimed MWh sales from that compliance year
within the relevant compliance filing, and that Staff has found this compliance helpful, and
recommends a similar directive be issued in this docket for compliance year 2026. (/d.)

7. Staff states that information submitted by Switch on behalf of its provider
demonstrates that Tenaska is in compliance with the requirements of the RPS for the Compliance
Year for the retail sales made to Switch, and that Staff has verified that the Annual Report
contains the reporting information required by NAC 704.8879(2). (/d.)

Commission Discussion and Findings

8. The Commission finds that it is in the public interest to accept Staff's
recommendations: to find that Switch is facilitating Tenaska’s compliance with the RPS for the
Compliance Year by retiring a specified number of PECs for their respective retail sales to
Switch.

9. Additionally, the Commission will issue the directive requested by Staff.

///
//1

///

Docket No. 26-04015 Page 4

Therefore, it is ordered:

1. The Annual Report filed by Switch Ltd. on behalf of Tenaska Power Services Co.
designated as Docket No. 26-04015, is approved.

2. Switch Ltd. facilitated Tenaska Power Services Co.’s compliance with the
renewable portfolio standard for compliance year 2025 for its sales to Switch Ltd.
Directive

3. Switch Ltd. shall, on behalf of Tenaska Power Services Co., provide with its 2026
renewable portfolio standard compliance year filing copies of its invoices that show the monthly
megawatt hours purchased in compliance year 2026 or other verification to support the megawatt
hours sold and used to compute the renewable portfolio standard compliance for compliance year
2026.
